problem.statement: Reviews with release r1 got 13 of 40 development reviews wrong: type_changed×3, field_removed×4, field_renamed×3, required_added×2, enum_value_removed×1.

hypothesis: If interface_compat blocks only changes that stop a previously valid value or record from being valid (a type swapped or narrowed, a field removed or renamed, a field made required, an enum value removed, a constraint tightened, a oneOf/anyOf alternative dropped) and makes widening changes advisory (type widened or made nullable, a required field made optional, an explicit type added that the existing enum already satisfies, a format added, oneOf/anyOf alternatives added, a draft-4 exclusive flag relaxed), then the share of held-out safe changes blocked will drop from 0.10 to 0.05 or less (no more than incumbent + 0.05). Breaking changes approved should stay near 0, because every breaking class seen in dev and in observed failures (type swap, field removed, field renamed, required added, enum value removed) is still blocked.
expected_benefit: Fewer approved breaking changes, with safe changes still approved.
possible_regressions: Each review runs one more step

I don't know which safe class caused the 10% false-alarm rate. My leading guesses are type widening/nullable and required -> optional, and I relaxed several possible causes at once. Each relaxation trades some risk of approving breaking changes for fewer false alarms.
The dev set has no cases of type widening, required -> optional, format addition, oneOf/anyOf edits, or draft-4 exclusive flags, so none of the new branches is exercised by `node check.mjs`.
Ad-hoc execution beyond `node check.mjs` was denied, so the new code paths (covers/valueType, the composition handling) have not been run against hand-built inputs.

change.summary: Revised candidate/validators/interface_compat.mjs in place. (1) Type check: it now blocks only when a type that was allowed before is no longer allowed (integer counts as covered by number). A pure widening, such as adding a type or making a field nullable, is now advisory 'type_widened'. (2) Adding an explicit type to a field that had only enum/const is advisory when every existing value already has that type. Before, any newly stated type blocked. (3) Making a required field optional (required_removed) is now advisory instead of blocking. (4) A newly added format is advisory. Changing one format or unit value to another still blocks. (5) A draft-4 boolean exclusiveMinimum/Maximum blocks only when it goes from false or absent to true. Relaxing it is advisory. (6) oneOf/anyOf: adding alternatives is advisory. Dropping or changing an alternative, or adding a new oneOf/anyOf, still blocks. Removing the keyword is advisory. Any change to allOf, not or $ref still blocks. I updated the header comment to match. Result of `node check.mjs`: 60 cases, accuracy 1.0, 0 of 38 breaking changes approved, 0 of 22 safe changes blocked, no errors. Limitation: running anything other than `node check.mjs` was denied in this environment, so I could not run ad-hoc tests of the new widening branches. They are checked by reading the code only, not by execution.
